He was succeeded by his eldest son, the second Baronet, who was also a painter.  The title became extinct on his death in 1926.

It was painted by the Pre-Raphaelite artist John Everett Millais (1829–1896) during 1853–54.  John Ruskin was an early advocate of the Pre-Raphaelite group of artists and part of their success was due to his efforts.
The Long Engagement | The Long Engagement is a painting by the Pre-Raphaelite artist Arthur Hughes which was created between 1854 and 1859.  The painting was originally titled Orlando.
